title: I went from zero coding to a fully automated Polymarket BTC bot. Here's what 2 years taught me
author: Quick-Designer-7205
selftext:
Two years ago I couldn't code. I had to learn VS Code, then what an environment even is, then how to write simple scripts, and I kept peeling the onion back from there.

My first bot ran on Hyperliquid. Then I moved to Polymarket. I've spent thousands of hours and a lot of money on lost profit and bad ideas. Ive quit or stopped many time. Mostly because i kept losing and didnt wamt to constsntly keep my computer running. Than i learned about VPS serverd and it wss back ok LOL. So

Here's what I've learned, the Up/down markets are some of the most efficient markets I've found.

Backtests are never the same as live. Fills, spreads, and timing eat whatever looked great on paper.

Technical strategies didn't work for me. So I stopped trying to be clever on paper and now test ideas live with small amounts.

The hardest part isn't the code, it's patience. A bot needs hours, days, weeks, and months of live data, and I know myself: if I get bored, I'll scrap a possibly winning idea too early. So I automated everything. Every hourly trade and my daily P&L gets posted to X and YouTube automatically, wins and losses, with every buy shown. It keeps me accountable and busy while the bot cooks.  I'm not claiming it works yet. It's a live experiment. I am 0 for 1000 so this might be the one.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: 'backtests are never the same as live' is the lesson everyone pays the most for. posting every trade publicly, losses too, is a smart trick, it's a lot harder to quietly kill a rule early when the whole run is on YouTube.

comments.author: Quick-Designer-7205
comments.body:
The learning curve is massive too. I was pumping out huge roi backtests when I first got in the game than realized my data was 2 second snap shots lol.  I only do polymakret have 250ms data now but there is a site that offers tons of backtest data for 100ms. Polybacktest, I think. Its on X. 

I saw a quote might help people trying to build. Worry about the risk management not the huge profits.

comments.author: pigeon_shit
comments.body:
Mate, forget the strategy stuff for a second, how are your socials performing? I recently thought about expanding my “project” to include socials and even some potential monetization… 

Back to your bot - I’ve learned a lot of the same things. I’m sure you ran into the “finding luck” dilemma too. I’m currently working on that part myself. Looking good so far, need another few weeks of data. TLDR - It’s okay to be lucky as long as the luck is persistent right? That’s my edge without tipping my hat too much. 

Anyway I actually believe you typed your post so that’s cool and I’m interested in your journey.

replies.author: Quick-Designer-7205
replies.body:
I just decided to step into throwing my bot on socials. There is so much fake Ai slope on X its a joke. But on there an YT now. Don't care if people follow i enjoyed learning how to do it and automate it. 

Luck is the name of the game. No other way. I am blow away by how efficient the 5, 15 1hr btc up down markets are. Its almost scary.  Stay lucky more than you are not and its all good. Lol

Also do the socials.  Gives you time away from the bot.

replies.author: pigeon_shit
replies.body:
Copy pasted from my project - 

**The problem:** most trading ideas look great until real money touches them. People fool themselves by changing the rules after they see the results.

**The league:** dozens of robot players compete every day with pretend money in simulated accounts. Every result is written down so nobody can change it later. Robot scouts watch but don't play. Most robots never make it, and that's the point.

**The real-money team:** I wrote the rulebook once, ahead of time. A robot only gets called up after it proves it can follow the rules. Once it's up, robot referees check every move, and a built-in loss limit benches the team if things go bad.

replies.author: Quick-Designer-7205
replies.body: Ok but you yourself know that paper and real are going to different by a decent margin. Is this in theory like a funded account if it advances. % of profits goto creator of the bots in the league ?

replies.author: pigeon_shit
replies.body:
Yeah there is variance for sure. So to hope to address this - if the live buy is off from the paper account by X%, the order is is cancelled/unfulfilled and marked as “dirty.” So yeah that means I’ll miss plays all the time… 

This is a funded account which uses whichever “scout” is currently promoted based off my predetermined/locked rules
